takeaway: Branches of the subclavian artery, 'vitamin C and D': vertebral, internal thoracic, thyrocervical trunk, costocervical trunk, dorsal scapular artery.

lines.text: Which artery is a direct branch of the subclavian artery?
Remember its branches with the mnemonic: vitamin C and D.
lines.say: (laugh) Remember its branches with the mnemonic: vitamin C and D.

lines.text: I is the internal thoracic artery: that is our answer.
Then come the thyrocervical trunk and the costocervical trunk.
And D is the dorsal scapular artery.
The other options are not on this list, so they are not direct branches of the subclavian artery.
So the answer is the internal thoracic artery.
